## **About 12126 PRAGATI EXPRESS**

## 12126 PRAGATI EXPRESS: Train Route, Schedule and Timings

PRAGATI EXPRESS runs between Pune Junction and C Shivaji Mah T Railway Station. Regarding PRAGATI EXPRESS timings, this train departs at 07:45 AM from the source station to arrive at the destination station at 11:25 AM . Total duration of the train from Pune Junction to C Shivaji Mah T Railway Station is 3 hrs 40 mins . PRAGATI EXPRESS runs from Pune Junction on 7 days a week ( Friday, Monday, Saturday, Sunday, Thursday, Tuesday, Wednesday ). There are 7 stoppages between Pune Junction and C Shivaji Mah T Railway Station .

PRAGATI EXPRESS route covers [Lonavala(LNL)](https://www.goibibo.com/trains/lonavala-railway-station-lnl-stn/), [Karjat(KJT)](https://www.goibibo.com/trains/karjat-railway-station-kjt-stn/), [Panvel(PNVL)](https://www.goibibo.com/trains/panvel-railway-station-pnvl-stn/), [Thane(TNA)](https://www.goibibo.com/trains/thane-railway-station-tna-stn/), [Dadar Central(DR)](https://www.goibibo.com/trains/mumbai-dadar-central-railway-station-dr-stn/). Finally, it arrives at C Shivaji Mah T Railway Station. It covers the distance of 118 KM km in 3 hrs 40 mins .

### About Pune

Nestled in the heart of Maharashtra, Pune is a city that beautifully blends the old with the new. Known for its rich cultural heritage and modern lifestyle, Pune is often referred to as the 'Queen of the Deccan'. The city is a bustling hub of academia, with numerous prestigious universities and colleges earning it the moniker 'Oxford of the East'. Pune's vibrant culture, historical significance, and scenic beauty make it a must-visit destination for travelers.

Whether you're exploring its ancient forts, attending a classical music concert, or indulging in local delicacies, Pune offers a unique experience that caters to all kinds of travelers. The city's historical landmarks, such as the Shaniwar Wada and Aga Khan Palace, tell tales of its glorious past, while its modern infrastructure and lively nightlife reflect its contemporary spirit. Pune is also known for its spiritual centers, including the Osho International Meditation Resort, which attracts visitors from around the world seeking peace and tranquility.

**Best Time to Visit**

Pune enjoys a moderate climate throughout the year, making it a pleasant destination to visit any time. However, the best time to explore Pune is from July to March. During these months, the weather is cool and comfortable, ideal for sightseeing and outdoor activities. The monsoon season, from July to September, brings lush greenery and a refreshing atmosphere, perfect for nature lovers. The winter months, from October to March, are particularly enjoyable with mild temperatures and clear skies, making it the peak tourist season.

Summers in Pune, from April to June, can be hot and dry, but the evenings are usually pleasant. If you prefer fewer crowds and lower accommodation rates, visiting during the off-peak summer season might be a good option.

**Places to Explore in Pune**

Pune is a treasure trove of attractions that cater to diverse interests. History enthusiasts can explore the majestic Shaniwar Wada, a historic fortification that offers a glimpse into the Maratha Empire. The Aga Khan Palace, another significant landmark, is not only an architectural marvel but also a site of historical importance where Mahatma Gandhi was imprisoned.

For adventure seekers, Sinhagad Fort provides thrilling trekking trails and panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Religious sites such as the Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati Temple, Pataleshwar Cave Temple, and Chaturshringi Temple offer spiritual solace and architectural beauty. The National War Museum is a must-visit for those interested in India's military history.

Don't miss the Osho International Meditation Resort, a serene haven for those looking to rejuvenate their mind and body. Pune's vibrant markets, such as Laxmi Road and Fergusson College Road, are perfect for shopping and experiencing the local culture.

**Airport Details**

Pathetic hotel. Stayed here for 1 night with family in January 2017. Over the counter booking. Rs. 1800 for 2 non-ac double rooms. 1 room was very very small. Rooms & washrooms were not so clean. There was lots of dust on sides of bed & below the mattress. Service was worst. The hotel has a restaurant at 1st floor. It was already late & the restaurant was suppose to close so we decided to have dinner in our rooms but the owner told us that we have to pay 15% extra for serving the food in room. It was a surprise for us. I stayed in hundreds of hotels in different cities but no hotel has this type of condition. His justification was that if you have dinner in rooms than there will be some spilling etc hence to clean & maintain that they charge 15% extra. I was in total shock. So to save 15% I told them to pack the food as parcel & just give us plates & spoons but to that also they refused & instructed the room boys not to provide anything. All hotels provide plates, glasses & spoons to their guests on request. It is an amenity. Even non-restaurant hotels provide these things on request. On too much request the room boy provided only spoons but they were dirty & not washed at all. Finally we used the paper plates which we had with us & had the food with our hands. The food was not even packed in containers but in polythene covers. My first pathetic experience like this.

Even for this kind of hotel the owner was praising about his hotel like there is no hotel in whole India like this. He told me that at this rate you cannot find any hotel in India as good as his hotel. I don't have any words to tell him at that time.

Just 1 day back we stayed at Hotel Sai Bansi in Shirdi & just for Rs. 900 (got good offer with MMT) for 2 ac rooms. Beautiful property, clean rooms, prompt service, good restaurant with all amenities. In fact it was also late night check-in so on our request they kept our food packed at the reception & provided us plates, spoons, glasses etc in the rooms with just 1 call. This is called professional hotel management.

Stayed at Hotel Radhika Palace, Parbhani as we didn't had any other choice at that time otherwise cannot stay at place like this.

My humble request to owner to check other cities's hotels & improve please. Be professional.

I've travelled a lot, and this place has to be the worst place we ever stayed in. We booked an AC room. We checked in at 9 pm, so the booking should have run until 9 pm the following day, since this is the hotel policy.

These were the issues we had. In the more expensive AC room:

1\. The floor wasn't swept

2\. There was a thick layer of dust on the side tables etc

3\. The bathroom was filthy - with a layer of sticky gunk on the sink and toilet. It is obvious this hadn't been washed.

4\. I gagged on the smell of the bedsheets - obvious it hadn't been washed

5\. Towels and sheets were stained

We had two children with us, so we asked for two extra mattresses, which we paid extra for. The staff put the mattresses on the floor, put bedsheets, then WALKED OVER the newly-made bed, leaving filthy shoe stains. They did not bother to replace the bedsheets, and they did not apologize.

We had a wedding to go to the following morning, and my husband wasn't sure if we'd stay at the wedding or come back for the afternoon, so my husband left the luggage at the reception with clear instructions to not give our room away (since it was paid for till 9:00 p.m.).

We come back, and sure enough, the AC room is given away. The hotel manager couldn't deny that we still had a reservation, so he offered to put us up in a non-AC room. It was very very hot, so we asked if there were AC rooms available. The manager said all the rooms were taken. When the assistant said the AC suite was still available - the manager blatantly cut him off, telling us a long, involved story about how this suite was reserved just that very morning.

So we were shoved into a really small non-AC bedroom with no extra child mattresses that we had already paid for. It was brutally hot, the room had absolutely no air circulation.

You'd be better off sleeping on the footpath.
